title: Product Detail Photos: Close-Ups of Texture | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one sharp photo into a close-up of stitching, grain, hardware or finish. AI product detail photos for listing galleries and paid social ads.
h1: Close-Up Product Detail Photos of Stitching, Grain, and Finish
lead: A wide catalog shot hides stitching, grain and hardware. Turn one sharp source into a close-up that answers the quality question.

steps.d: Use a steady, well-lit photo in which the stitching, texture or clasp is visible. That feature becomes the close-up subject.
Name one feature to enlarge and one simple setting. You get a square image where the detail fills the frame.
Download the close-up, check color and construction against the source, then place it after the hero shot.

faq.q: Which product details work well in close-up?
faq.a: Materials, stitching, clasps, zippers, rims and finishes answer quality questions that a wide product shot cannot.

faq.q: How close should the source photo be?
faq.a: Keep the feature sharp with enough surrounding product to show where it sits. One close-up should answer one detail question.

faq.q: Where should a detail photo go?
faq.a: Place it after the full product image in a listing gallery, carousel or social post built around one quality point.

faq.q: How do I get a sharp close-up?
faq.a: A clear, steady, well-lit source gives the generated detail the best chance of staying readable.

faq.q: Can the macro shot be used on a listing?
faq.a: Yes. It supports the main image by showing material or construction details in a product gallery.

faq.q: What does a detail photo cost?
faq.a: Each AI product detail photo costs 24 credits, shown before the job starts.

faq.q: Can the close-up replace the main product photo?
faq.a: No. Keep the full-product hero first, then use the close-up where shoppers inspect quality.

faq.q: Do I need a macro lens or professional camera?
faq.a: No. A sharp phone photo can be the source; the close-up is generated from it and the download has no watermark.

steps.prompt: Show the uploaded wallet’s stitched edge and grain in a crisp square close-up.
